La vidalita, del norte argentino y triste, la recuperaron en los noventa jóvenes como Mayte Martín; la milonga pampeana la trajo Pepa Oro en compás de tangos, Chacón la remataba por tanguillos y Pepe de la Matrona la grabó. Hay dos discos fundamentales: Cantes de ida y vuelta (Junta de Andalucía, 1985, con Menese, José Mercé y Luis de Córdoba) y Dos mundos cantan (Expo 92, con Valderrama, Rocío Jurado y Chano Lobato).

scenes.name: Las saetas
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Cante dolido que solo se canta en Semana Santa, al paso de las imágenes, a palo seco o con cornetas y tambores, por martinetes, siguiriyas (las más comunes), soleares, cañas o polos, con coplas de exaltación religiosa que exigen gran potencia de voz. Nace a finales del XIX en Cádiz: Enrique el Mellizo y sus hijos detenían al Nazareno desde los cuatro balcones de su casa con sus saetas. A él se atribuye la saeta por siguiriyas, que desarrolló Manuel Centeno en el siglo XX. Manuel Torre, el Niño Gloria, la Niña de los Peines, Manolo Caracol y Antonio Mairena eran esperados en Semana Santa para cantarlas sin amplificación desde un balcón a la altura de las imágenes; Manuel Mairena grabó un vía crucis entero. Un equipo francés grabó en directo a los saeteros de Jerez, Arcos y Lebrija en la Semana Santa de 1993 para la colección Flamenco vivo.

scenes.name: Demófilo y los Machado
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Antonio Machado y Álvarez, Demófilo, fue el primer autor español que dedicó un libro entero al flamenco: la Colección de cantes flamencos recogidos y anotados (1881), piedra angular de la flamencología moderna; escribió también sobre las saetas y dirigió la revista El Folclore Andaluz (1882-1883). Sus hijos, los poetas Antonio y Manuel Machado (autor de Cante hondo), heredaron la afición, y sus coplas se cantan a menudo sin que los cantaores sepan que son versos cultos. Calixto Sánchez dedicó a Antonio Machado un disco en 2001, y José Menese hizo suyas las letras de Francisco Moreno Galván.

scenes.name: La farruca y el garrotín
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Cantes aflamencados de fuera de Andalucía. La farruca, gallega, llegó a Cádiz con los comerciantes gallegos del XIX y es más baile que cante; la popularizó Manuel Torre a principios del XX y hoy casi solo la canta Pepe Menese, con una letra de Moreno Galván que se hizo himno en la Transición. Su baile, viril, lo creó Faíco; Carmen Amaya lo bailó vestida de hombre, Falla lo incluyó en El sombrero de tres picos y la versión de Antonio Gades en la película de Los Tarantos, la última de Carmen Amaya, se enseña hoy en las academias. El garrotín viene del folclore asturiano y lo hicieron suyo los gitanos de Lleida; lo difundieron Carmen Amaya y la Niña de los Peines, que lo cantaba con aire de tangos, Faíco hizo sus coreografías y Blas Vega recogió una copla antigua cantada por el Chaparro en la Magna antología del cante flamenco.

scenes.name: Los fandangos de Huelva
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Huelva reclama la cuna del fandango andaluz y es la provincia con más estilos: las antologías recogen más de treinta y cinco, locales (Encinasola, el Alosno, Cabezas Rubias, Calañas, el Andévalo, Valverde del Camino) y personales, creados por profesionales como Paco Isidro, Pepe Rebollo, el Comía, Antonio Rengel, Pérez de Guzmán y Paco Toronjo; de fuera dejaron su sello el Gloria, Macandé, el Carbonerillo y Manolo Caracol. Paco Toronjo, fijo en los festivales desde finales de los sesenta y en las bienales de Sevilla, les dio una jondura difícil de imitar. El baile, de pareja y galanteo, se ve ya poco.

scenes.name: Los cantes de Levante o de las minas
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Nacidos del trabajo en las minas del siglo XIX en las sierras de Cartagena y La Unión y en Linares, La Carolina y Andújar: cantes de dolor profundo sobre la mina, sus accidentes y los compañeros muertos, hechos con fandangos regionales, murcianas, malagueñas y el cante de madrugá de los mineros. La taranta, el más significativo, tiene dos estilos, el de Linares (Gabriel Moreno, Carmen Linares) y el de La Unión (Encarnación Fernández, Pepe Cros), y Camarón le puso dulzura; el taranto, almeriense, tiene compás porque nació para el baile de Carmen Amaya en los cuarenta, con el Ciego de la Playa y Pedro el Morato. La cartagenera, de temas más urbanos, la fijó Antonio Chacón a finales del XIX y la cantaron Cayetano Muriel, Manuel Centeno, Manuel Torre y la Niña de los Peines. La minera se atribuye a Rojo el Alpargatero, Antonio Grau Mora, que hacia 1885 abrió en La Unión una posada que acabó en café cantante y oía cantar a los mineros de madrugada: es el gran creador de los cantes mineros. Las granaínas, de Frasquito Yerbabuena y sobre todo Chacón, son un cante casi barroco hoy cargado de vibratos operísticos. Sin minas, los concursos de Linares y La Unión mantienen vivos estos cantes.

scenes.name: Las cantiñas: alegrías, caracoles, mirabrás y romeras
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Cantes alegres de la bahía de Cádiz, en compás de soleá y muy ligados al baile, que arranca majestuoso y va ganando fuerza hasta desplantes electrizantes. Nacen probablemente de la jotilla gaditana, hermanada con la jota aragonesa por la resistencia común contra Napoleón, de ahí las letras sobre la guerra y el mar; la leyenda atribuye su creación a Enrique el Mellizo, que oyó a una muchacha cantar jotas con un ciego. Tomaron identidad en la segunda mitad del XIX. Hay cantiñas del Pinini de Utrera y Lebrija y de Córdoba; la rosa ya no se canta. Las alegrías, al principio baile de mujer sola, se hicieron más lentas a comienzos del XX y empiezan con el «tirititrán» que, según Chano Lobato, inventó Pericón de Cádiz al olvidar la letra; las cantaron el Mellizo, Ignacio Ezpeleta, Aurelio Sellés, Manolo Vargas y Pericón. Los caracoles, de Tío José el Granaíno (picador del Chiclanero), los recreó Chacón y triunfaron en Madrid («la gran calle de Alcalá»). El mirabrás son alegrías largas (José Menese, con letras de Moreno Galván), y las romeras se atribuyen al Granaíno o a una cantaora llamada la Romera. Hoy el gran intérprete es Chano Lobato.

scenes.name: Los tangos, tientos y marianas
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Con bulerías y cantiñas, el gran cante festero: letras de vida, amor y muerte con cierta ligereza, ritmo vivo y pegadizo fácil de seguir con palmas, y un baile sensual. Cádiz y Sevilla se disputan su paternidad, pero los hay en toda Andalucía y en Extremadura; Triana tiene el estilo del Titi y Jerez su propio sello. Su origen musical se discute: Mairena los tenía por cante básico gitano; los estudios recientes los llevan a Cuba y las habaneras llegadas a Sevilla y Cádiz en la segunda mitad del XIX; los granadinos defienden una raíz morisca (el disco Granada canta por tangos recoge trece estilos, entre ellos los de la morería). Manuel Ríos Ruiz concluye que no se sabe con certeza. La Niña de los Peines se hizo inmortal con su copla «Péinate tú con mis peines». Del tango nacen los tientos, más pausados y solemnes, que cantaron primero el Mellizo y el Marrurro y se popularizaron a comienzos del XX, y la mariana, que difundió Bernardo el de los Lobitos y hoy casi solo canta Pepe Menese con letras de Moreno Galván.

scenes.name: Las soleares
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: La madre del cante y uno de sus pilares, independiente de cualquier otro ritmo; los cantaores la consideran «el toro bravo del arte jondo». Coplas solemnes y sentenciosas de tres o cuatro octosílabos, unidas por la guitarra, que suelen rematarse por bulerías; muy apropiadas para el baile de mujer. Se desarrolló al sur del Guadalquivir desde los jaleos festivos: la primera mención es de la Andonda en Triana hacia 1840, una cantaora temible contemporánea del Fillo, y tomó su forma actual entre 1875 y 1915. Las mujeres fueron clave en su creación y transmisión (la Andonda, Mercedes la Serneta, Fernanda de Utrera, Carmen Linares). Hay soleares de Triana (la Andonda, Silverio, Fernando el de Triana, la Niña de los Peines, Tomás Pavón, Mairena), de Alcalá, más solemnes (Joaquín el de la Paula, Juan Talega), de Utrera (la Serneta, el Pinini, María Peña, Fernanda), de Cádiz y el Puerto, más jondas (Enrique Butrón, el Mellizo, Paquirri el Guanté), de Jerez, breves y llenas de melismas (Curro Frijones, José Illanda, Juan Mojama, Tío José de Paula, Manuel Torre) y de Córdoba, más pausadas.

scenes.name: Las siguiriyas, livianas y serranas
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Una de las expresiones más dramáticas y de los palos más importantes: sin siguiriyas y soleares el flamenco no sería lo que es. Un quejío entero de lamentos que no admite medias tintas («con las siguiriyas no se puede vender la burra»), con coplas trágicas de cuatro versos (6, 6, 10 y 6 sílabas), muchas sobre la muerte de los seres queridos, y falsetas lentas que suenan a campanas a muerto. Lorca la describió como un grito terrible que divide el paisaje en dos; Tía Anica la Piriñaca decía que cuando la cantaba a gusto la boca le sabía a sangre. La cantaban ya el Planeta (la de la Luna, la más antigua conocida) y el Fillo; luego Manuel Torre, Silverio, Paco la Luz, Cagancho, el Nitri, Curro Dulce, el Loco Mateo, el Mellizo, Terremoto de Jerez (que cantó toda la noche por siguiriyas con su madre muerta en brazos) y Juan Talega; hoy el Chocolate y José Menese. Antonio Mairena grabó unas cuarenta y cinco formas: es el siguiriyero más importante. Sus escuelas son Jerez y los Puertos, Cádiz y Triana. En el baile la difundió Vicente Escudero y Pilar López le añadió los palillos. La liviana, cante de campo, caminos y bandoleros, prepara la voz para la serrana, a la que Silverio dio brillo y con la que se remata por siguiriyas.

scenes.name: La caña, el polo y la petenera
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Tres cantes de la familia de la soleá. La caña, con ayes más arrastrados, se sitúa en la serranía de Ronda (un viajero inglés la oyó allí en 1830) o en la voz árabe gaunia, «canción»; la cantaron el Fillo, Tío José el Granaíno, Antonio Chacón, Pepe de la Matrona y Rafael Romero el Gallina, y hoy se usa más para el baile solemne. El polo se cantaba tras la caña, con la misma métrica; el de Tobalo, su supuesto creador, aparece ya en Estébanez Calderón y hoy se usa en la soleá apolá; Enrique Morente grabó el de Chacón. La petenera, melancólica y de origen incierto, se atribuye a una mujer de Paterna de la Ribera, «la perdición de los hombres», o a los sefardíes de los Balcanes; los gitanos la evitaron porque traía mala suerte. La cantaron la Niña de los Peines, Naranjito de Triana, Rafael Romero, Fosforito y hoy Pepe Menese.

scenes.name: Los cantes de Málaga: malagueñas, rondeñas, jaberas y verdiales
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Después de Sevilla y Cádiz, Málaga es la provincia con más variedad de cantes. La malagueña, cante libre, sin medida y sin baile, de rico toque, ha influido en las granaínas y en todos los cantes minero-levantinos. Nació en Álora (las malagueñas perotas) a partir de los fandangos abandolaos, acompañados de bandola; tras los anónimos y los de Cipriano Pitana, Francisco Jiménez y Joaquín Tabaco, Juan Breva le dio identidad propia, y Lorca escribió de su trino. Su esplendor es la segunda mitad del XIX, con el Canario, la Trini, Baldomero Pacheco y Fosforito el Viejo; también firmaron malagueñas el Mellizo, único gitano creador de una (inspirada en el prefacio de la misa), y Chacón. Diego Clavel recogió treinta y una en los noventa. La rondeña, de principios del XIX y de la tierra del Tobalo, es la pieza con que muchos guitarristas abren sus conciertos; la jabera, ruda y difícil, debe su nombre a una vendedora de habas y está casi perdida; los verdiales, de probable raíz morisca, apenas han cambiado y conservan la panda con violín, panderos, chinchines y cañas para la fiesta de san Juan.

scenes.name: Los tanguillos de Cádiz
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Vinculados al carnaval de Cádiz, son el soporte de chirigotas, coros y murgas; cantados en grupo pierden su naturaleza flamenca, que es individual, aunque como baile la conservan. Hay constancia de los «tangos graciosos» del barrio de La Viña en 1779, en la tonadilla La anónima de Tomás Abril, y el tango americano o de negros terminó de formarlos. Letras jocosas y satíricas: «el chiste ingenuo y feliz enfrente de la tragedia jonda del quejío» (Emilio Jiménez Díaz). Aurelio y Pericón de Cádiz, Manuel Vargas y la Perla los grabaron en la primera mitad del siglo XX, y hasta Mairena dejó dos. Chano Lobato, su mayor cultor, los elevó a cante noble y recrea la venta de los cuadros que popularizó Pericón.

scenes.name: Las tonás: martinetes, carceleras y deblas
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Cantes sin acompañamiento, prueba de su antigüedad, en cuartetas octosílabas de intensa carga dramática y origen gitano indiscutible: son crónicas de la miseria, la cárcel y la persecución. Demófilo ya las daba en 1881 por «cantes viejos casi caídos en desuso»; en el siglo XIX hubo entre veintisiete y treinta y cuatro, cada una con el nombre de su creador. La más antigua es la de Tío Luis el de la Juliana, aguador y primer cantaor del que hay noticia (segunda mitad del siglo XVIII), conservada por Antonio Chacón y recreada por Pepe de la Matrona; se le atribuye también la toná de los pajaritos, que recuerda la tonada sefardí de los bilbilicos. Los martinetes toman el nombre del martillo de la fragua, aunque es difícil cantar mientras se forja: Tío Juane de Jerez montaba una fragua en escena en los setenta y ochenta, y Antonio el Bailarín creó su baile con martillo y yunque; la familia fragüera más antigua es la de los Cantorales de Cádiz, que Silverio visitaba. Las carceleras cantan la prisión y servían para pasar mensajes en romaní desde las rejas. La debla, único palo con nombre romaní («diosa»), es religiosa, casi perdida y muy difícil; llegó a hoy por Tomás Pavón en los cuarenta y la recuperó Antonio Mairena.

scenes.name: Las sevillanas
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Nacen de las seguidillas castellanas, que en Sevilla se hicieron más vivas y fáciles de repetir: cuatro coplas para bailar en pareja un galanteo, con temas andaluces, amorosos o rocieros (corraleras, rocieras, bíblicas, de feria, marineras, romeras). Lorca recogió una del siglo XVIII. Su gran auge comercial llegó en los setenta, con millones de discos que daban envidia a los flamencos; las han grabado con jondura Manuel Vallejo, la Niña de los Peines, la Paquera de Jerez, el Turronero, Chiquetete y Camarón.

scenes.name: El fandango
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Muy apreciado por su musicalidad y fácil de interpretar, no es un palo básico pero no es menor: la vieja división entre cantes grandes y chicos está obsoleta, y la jondura la pone el intérprete, no la antigüedad del palo. Canto para bailar de origen muy antiguo e incierto (Corominas lo deriva del portugués fado; hay quien le ve un lejano origen árabe), aparece por escrito en un entremés de 1705 y lo describe el deán Manuel Martí en 1712; en el siglo XIX fue el cante y baile nacional español, y a finales de siglo se aflamencó en Andalucía y dejó de bailarse. De él salen las granaínas, las malagueñas y los cantes de Levante, y hay fandangos propios en Lucena, Cabra, Puente Genil, Jaén, Granada o Almería. Su apogeo en la ópera flamenca lo desprestigió tanto que a cantaores como Pepe Menese les parece un insulto que se lo pidan; desde los años ochenta se revaloriza.

facts.title: First MTV Metal Video (1981)
facts.body: Iron Maiden's "Wrathchild" was the first metal song video shown on MTV, appearing as the 70th video in the channel's initial rotation after its launch on August 1st, 1981. This marked heavy metal's early presence on the nascent music video network. "The first metal song was Wrath Child by Aaron Maiden at number 70."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The Rise and Fall and Future of the Music Video - Part 1
facts.name: Metal

facts.title: First MTV Punk Video (1981)
facts.body: The Ramones' "Do You Remember Rock and Roll Radio?" was the first punk song video shown on MTV, appearing as the 105th video in the channel's initial library after its launch on August 1st, 1981. This marked punk rock's early representation on the new music video network. "And the first punk song was Do You Remember Rock and Roll Radio by the Ramones at number 105?"
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The Rise and Fall and Future of the Music Video - Part 1
facts.name: Punk

facts.title: Stolen Briefcase (Portland, March 22, 1981) – 70 Pages of U2 Lyrics; Returned 23 Years Later
facts.body: After a show at the Foghorn bar in Portland, Oregon, on March 22, 1981, three groupies visited backstage. After they left, Bono realized one had taken his briefcase containing $300 cash, his visa card in his real name Paul Hewson, tour documents, photos, fan letters, personal correspondence from his wife, and notebooks holding 70 pages of lyrics destined for U2's second album — material that had taken three years to accumulate. The resulting crisis forced Bono to improvise most of the lyrics for the *October* album in the studio, which is widely held to explain that album's unfinished quality. In 2003, a woman from Olympia, Washington, named Danielle Ruyom contacted U2: her friend Cindy Harris had found the briefcase's contents in the attic of a house she'd purchased in Tacoma. After a year of negotiations through multiple layers of U2 management, they met Bono on October 20, 2004, and returned everything except the cash and the briefcase itself. "The only thing that was really missing was the case itself."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: U2

facts.title: Rap Diss as a Live Medium (1981)
facts.body: Cool Mo Dee's live performance at the Harlem World Club in 1981, where he delivered "dazzling disses" against Busy B, established the rap diss as a significant live medium. This event, captured on tape, predated the widespread ignition of rap disses on wax. "Cool mode D's throwdown established the rap dis as a live medium."
facts.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
facts.name: hip hop

facts.title: Pioneering Pilot (1981)
facts.body: Gary Numan, a prominent figure in the new wave music scene, was not only an influential musician but also an accomplished pilot. In 1981, he successfully completed a flight around the world in his own aircraft, showcasing a remarkable adventurous spirit beyond his musical career. "Gary Newman, the new wave star, turned electronic icon to guys like Back in Dave Grohl, became very accomplished as a pilot, even working as a stunt pilot in air shows."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: New Wave

facts.title: Origin of Term - Mark Arm (1981)
facts.body: In 1981, Mark Arm of Mr. Epp and the Calculations used the word "Grunge" in a letter to the alternative weekly "Desperate Times" to describe his band's "pure noise" sound. This marks the first known appearance of the word in print as a descriptor for a specific music style from the American Pacific Northwest, although the term had existed in American slang to denote something repulsive. "This is the first known appearance of the word Grunge in print as a description for a certain style of music from the American Pacific Northwest."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: Peaked Too Soon - Bands That Were Ahead of Their Time

facts.title: Defining Sound of "Música Blanca" at Barraca (1981)
facts.body: Joy Division played a crucial role in shaping the "música blanca" aesthetic introduced by DJs Juan Santamaría and Carlos Simó at Barraca beginning in 1981. This innovative sound sought to distinguish itself from the popular funk and disco music, featuring rhythms that were exotic and largely unknown to the general public. "música blanca para distinguirse del fanco disco dominantes de la época, y que estaba definida por grupos como de Pech Mode, de Kyu, y un division o de Fall."
facts.source: Central Sonora
facts.episode: Cuando Valencia fue la capital mundial del Clubbing

facts.title: Vince Clark's Departure (December 1, 1981)
facts.body: On December 1, 1981, chief songwriter Vince Clark left Depeche Mode, believing the group had little future and that he could achieve greater success on his own. While his subsequent projects like Yazoo and Eurasia had hits, Depeche Mode's overall album sales (over 50 million) ultimately surpassed his post-band career. "The date was December 1, 1981. The first member and chief son writer Vince Clark decided that he wanted out. Why? Well, he didn't think the group had much of a future."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Depeche Mode

facts.title: Vince Clarke's Departure (December 1, 1981)
facts.body: On December 1, 1981, founding member and sole songwriter Vince Clarke announced his departure from Depeche Mode. His reason was a desire to be in a band that would focus solely on studio work and avoid touring. This decision left Depeche Mode without a primary songwriter, prompting a significant shift in the band's creative direction. "But on December 1st, 1981, Vince Clark, the band's sole songwriter, announced that he was quitting."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: From the Archives: The Top 100 Moments in New Rock - Part 3
facts.name: Depeche Mode

facts.title: Jovan Muske Perfume Sponsorship (1981)
facts.body: Decades after their initial commercial work, The Rolling Stones "raised eyebrows" by signing the first major tour sponsorship deal with Jovan Muske perfume in 1981. This action further illustrated their consistent alignment with aggressive commercial strategies, or "the hard sell." "They would raise eyebrows for signing the first major tourist sponsorship with Jovan Muske perfume."
facts.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
facts.episode: I’d Like to Teach the World to Buy Edition Part 1

facts.title: Early Formation and Evolution (1981-2010s)
facts.body: The Beastie Boys began in 1981 as a "goof" by three guys from well-to-do New York families, initially motivated by drinking beer and meeting women. Over three decades, they evolved from a hardcore punk band into esteemed members of the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, recognized as one of the most important acts of all time in two different genres, ultimately ceasing activity with the death of Adam Yauch. "When they finally had to call it quits when one of them died three decades later, they were esteemed members of the Rock and Wall Hall of Fame and considered to be one of the most important acts of all time in two different genres."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: The Beastie Boys

facts.title: Creative Control Conflict (1981)
facts.body: During the recording of *Rat Patrol from Fort Bragg* in 1981, founding member Mick Jones and Joe Strummer were in conflict over creative control. Jones, along with drummer Topper Heaton, was exploring Dub, Reggae, and world music, leading to longer songs, while Strummer disliked this direction and desired a concise, single album due to the band's debt with CBS. This led to them working in separate studios. "At the time, Mick Jones, the founder of the group, was fighting with Joe Strummer over creative control... it got to the point where Mick was working on material in one studio, and Joe was working on his clash material in another."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: The Clash

facts.title: Debt with Label (1981)
facts.body: The Clash had gone "deep into debt" with their label, CBS, which influenced Joe Strummer's desire for a "nice tight single album" for effective promotion, contrasting with Mick Jones's more sprawling vision for *Rat Patrol from Fort Bragg*. "after going deep into debt with their label, Joe wanted a nice tight single album that CBS could promote effectively."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: The Clash

facts.title: Re-engagement and Musical Influence (1981)
facts.body: After Carolyn Coon's management didn't work out, and neither did the company that followed, Bernie Rhodes was back managing The Clash in 1981, while also managing other bands like Dexys Midnight Runners. During this period, Rhodes notably convinced the band that 12-inch dance remixes were a beneficial idea, which led to the creation of the dance mix for "The Magnificent Seven."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: The Clash

facts.title: Bernie Rhodes' Re-hiring and Internal Strife (1981)
facts.body: Rhodes was re-hired in 1981 after the band was unsuccessfully managed by Joe Strummer's girlfriend. Upon his return, he actively worked to pit Joe Strummer and Mick Jones against each other, possibly with the goal of becoming the band's musical director. "But then he was re-hired in 1981 after the group was unsuccessfully run by Joe Stromer's girlfriend. And this is where things went wrong again."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: The Clash

facts.title: Third Wave's California Roots – Bay Area Uptones (1981) Inspired Hardcore + Ska Fusion; Secret Sauce for Third Wave
facts.body: The third wave began in the Bay Area with The Uptones (1981), a group of 15 and 16-year-olds fascinated by the Two-Tone sound. They played tons of Bay Area shows for seven years, inspiring other groups. The next generation added hardcore punk DNA to the mix — this was the secret sauce that set the stage for the third wave. Fishbone (formed 1979) also kept ska alive through the mid-1980s in California, mixing punk, funk, soul, metal, and ska with social commentary about racism, oppression, and nuclear war. "Hardcore punk rock. And this was the secret sauce that set things up for what would be the third wave of Scott."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

It played a significant role in MTV's early rotation, and its boldness is credited with paving the way for artists like Madonna in showcasing female sexuality and control. "The video today seems obviously very dated, but it was very daring for the time."

facts.title: Early Adoption of Compact Disc (1981-1985)
facts.body: Classical music aficionados and orchestra conductors, notably Herbert von Karajan, quickly embraced the Compact Disc in the early 1980s. facts.title: First Solo Album - KooKoo (1981)
facts.body: Debbie Harry recorded her solo debut album, *KooKoo*, in the first half of 1981 with Nile Rodgers and Bernard Edwards of the disco supergroup Chic. The album moved her further into "Black informed pop," featuring cutting-edge music like the dance hit "Backfire" and the breakbeat track "The Jam Was Moving." The album cover, an image by sci-fi/horror artist H.R. Giger depicting her face pierced with swords, was noted as "freaky." Despite its artistic ambition, *KooKoo* was not a commercial success, peaking at number 25 on the album chart, producing no Top 40 hits, and exiting the chart within three months. "It was the first sign that Blondie's imperial era was coming to a close."
facts.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
facts.episode: This Ain’t No Party! Edition Part 2
facts.name: Blondie

facts.title: Age of Consent Protocol on American Tours (Post-1981)
facts.body: During American tours after 1981, Duran Duran implemented a system to prevent legal issues related to sexual consent. Their daily itineraries included a code number at the bottom, which indicated the age of consent (18, 20, or 21) for the specific state they were in. This proactive measure aimed to avoid "awkward legal problems." "Those numbers signified the age of consent for whatever state they happen to be in."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Duran Duran

facts.title: Death in Miami (May 1981)
facts.body: On May 8, 1981, Bob Marley decided to return home to Jamaica and asked Chris Blackwell, head of Island Records, to fly him there. However, his vital signs worsened during the flight, forcing the plane to land in Miami, where he was taken to Cedars of Lebanon Hospital. Critically ill and in immense pain, he died on May 11, 1981, surrounded by his family and weighing only 82 pounds, at the age of 36. "He was critically ill and in a tremendous amount of pain. But there was nothing the doctors could do except offer large amounts of powerful pain killers. And then, surrounded by his family and weighing just 82 pounds, Bob Marley died. It was May 11, 1981."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Bob Marley

facts.title: Early Formation and Struggles (1981-1992)
facts.body: Pulp formed very young, around ages 15-16, in Sheffield, at roughly the same time as bands like Joy Division and Siouxsie and the Banshees, predating even New Order. Despite their early start, they struggled for approximately 15 years to achieve success, spending over a decade experimenting with various styles like New Wave, synthesizers, and Post-Punk, and releasing early albums on small, ineffective labels with poor or no critical reception. "Palt is a very curious group because although it was one of the pillars of Brit-Pop Palt was forming almost at the same time as groups like Joy Division or like Suixion de Bansis then."

facts.title: Commercial Peak and Fragmentation (1981-82)
facts.body: Technopop reached its commercial peak in the winter of 1981-82, characterized by its accessibility and danceability, with bands like The Human League, Duran Duran, and Depeche Mode gaining global hits. During this time, the genre began to fragment into various sounds, with some artists remaining fully electronic while others reintroduced standard rhythm sections. "The early 80s saw the biggest explosion in music-making technology since the arrival of the electric guitar 30 years earlier."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

facts.title: Gary Moffet on Canadian Inferiority Complex (1981)
facts.body: In 1981, Gary Moffet of April Wine articulated the ongoing "inferiority complex" in Canada regarding its own bands, criticizing the perception that Canadian artists needed to succeed in the US before being respected at home. He questioned why Canadian judgment wasn't trusted independently of American approval. "Gary Moffet of the band April Wine was still talking about the perception that Canadian bands needed to make it in the US even in 1981. He said Canada has an inferiority complex because of it. They don't trust their own bands with enough respect. They don't perceive you as being really big unless you go away, improve yourself in America. Why should you have to do well away from home before your own people consider you a top band? That's silly. Canadians should trust their own judgment. They shouldn't need America's approval about something before they accept it."
facts.source: For the Record - The 70s
facts.episode: Ep. 45 - Oh, Canada! Canada's Rock Music Industry in the 70s
facts.name: April Wine

facts.title: Post-Music Career and Death (1981)
facts.body: After enjoying success in the late 1940s and very early 1950s, Brown spent decades unable to secure a hit. He eventually began selling encyclopedias door-to-door, using the unique marketing tactic of offering autographed photos of himself in black neighborhoods. He continued to release occasional R&B records but earned more from his encyclopedia sales before his death in 1981. "He eventually started selling in Cyclopidia's door to door, with the unique gimmick that when he was in black neighborhoods, he could offer the people whose doors he was knocking on, a nautical raft photo of himself."

facts.body: The music video for this song from 1982 was noted for being slicker, glossier, and more expensive than earlier low-tech productions. Its sophisticated visual style significantly contributed to changing the very sound of new wave from its powerpop and post-punk roots to the emerging synthpop genre, marking a "changing of the guard" moment in the music industry. "By 1982, videos like The Human Leagues don't you want me, were not only Slicker, Glossier, and more expensive. They were changing the very sound of new wave from Powerpop and Postpunk to Synthpop."

facts.body: This 1980s new wave hit is an example of a song/band influenced by Donna Summer's "I Feel Love," with music journalist Simon Reynolds suggesting "the 1980s began with I Feel Love." "The music journalist Simon Reynolds said that the 1980s began with I Feel Love and when you consider the new wave music that was so prevalent in that era and you can hear it starting in I Feel Love, it's really hard to argue with him on that."

facts.body: This song, a romantic melodrama brought to life by Oakey and Sulley, was the last track and fourth single from the *Dare* album. Oakey initially thought it was "filler" and "NAF" and tried to dissuade his label, Virgin, from releasing it as a 45. However, Virgin commissioned their most expensive music video to date—a "meta-film noir" loosely based on *A Star Is Born*, making it the "highest gloss clip on MTV at the time." It reached UK number one in December 1981 (Christmas number one) and US number one in July 1982, after an 18-week climb, becoming their biggest hit on both sides of the Atlantic. "Oki thought the song was filler, he called it NAF, and he tried to dissuade his label, Virgin, from putting it out as a 45."
facts.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

facts.body: This album was released in 1981, a period when artificial intelligence was still considered science fiction. As one of the most technically minded groups of all time, their work often explored themes related to technology and machines, making this album a notable reference point for the early intersection of computers and music. "That's computer world from 1981. A time when artificial intelligence was nothing but science fiction."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The History and Future of AI in Music

facts.title: Futurist Conceptual Work
facts.body: This album was a futuristic conceptual work that accurately predicted the omnipresence of computing in daily life, anticipating digital communications after earlier albums explored terrestrial ones. It gained significant popularity in US ghettos and showcased Kraftwerk's continued leadership in electronic music, even as other electronic bands emerged. "En 1981 lanzaron Computer World, una obra conceptual futurista que predijo la omnipresencia de la informática en la vida cotidiana."
facts.source: Central Sonora
facts.episode: Por qué KRAFTWERK es la banda más influyente de la historia?
facts.name: Computer World

facts.title: Source of "The Tragically Hip" Name (1981)
facts.body: The name "The Tragically Hip" was taken from a line in a 1981 video collection of music and comedy produced by Mike Nesmith, a former member of The Monkees. The specific line was part of a skit about fundraising for "poor yuppies" to sustain their lifestyles of Lamborghinis and cocaine. "That was stolen from a line in a 1981 video collection of music and comedy by Mike Nessmith, ex of the monkeys. The skit had to do with raising money for poor yuppies to keep them in Lamborghini's and cocaine. They were the so-called tragically hip."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Michael Nesmith

facts.body: This song was a massive cultural phenomenon, topping the charts for 10 consecutive weeks from November 21, 1981, to January 23, 1982, spanning Thanksgiving, the holidays, and nearly Valentine's Day. Olivia Newton-John recorded it after Rod Stewart and Tina Turner passed on it, initially unsure about its daringly suggestive lyrics, which included lines like "There's nothing left to talk about unless it's horizontally." Her manager ultimately convinced her to record it, and its catchy tune, fitness-themed video (directed by Brian Grant), scorching guitar solo by Steve Lukather of Toto, and Olivia's playful yet sexual performance made it a career-defining and era-defining hit, closely associated with the 80s aerobics craze and MTV's early days. Foreigner's "Waiting For A Girl Like You" was blocked from the number one spot by "Physical" for nine weeks. "Let's get physical, physical. All I can, physical. Let's get physical. Let me fight it down."
facts.source: For the Record - The 70s

facts.title: First Popular Music Album on CD
facts.body: Pressed in August 1982, Abba's 1981 album "The Visitors" holds the distinction of being the first popular music album released on compact disc. "That honor went to Abba with their 1981 album The Visitors. It was pressed in August of 1982."

facts.title: First Pop Album on CD
facts.body: Released in late 1981, this album by ABBA holds the distinction of being the first pop music album launched on the Compact Disc format. Its release marked an early, albeit slow, step for the CD into the pop music market. "en 1981 a finales de año tuvimos el primer disco lanzado en disco compacto que fue de Aba de Visitors."

facts.name: The Visitors

facts.body: ABBA's album *The Visitors* was the first compact disc to be manufactured for public sale. This marked a significant milestone in the commercial launch and widespread availability of the CD format. "The first CD to be manufactured for public sale was The Visitors by Ava."

facts.title: MP3 Reference Track
facts.body: This song was penned by Suzanne Vega in 1981 while at Tom's Restaurant, located at 2880 Broadway in New York City, a location also famously featured on the television show "Seinfeld." Its unique characteristics—being a pure a cappella recording with almost no reverb—made it an ideal reference track for the Fraunhofer Institute in Germany during the development of the MP3 compression algorithm. Engineers on the project meticulously listened to the song "tens of thousands of times" as they worked to compress the digital audio file to one-tenth its original size without introducing audible glitches, ultimately achieving a very good result. "Now I played that song because it was used as a reference track when the Fraunhofer Institute in Germany was working on creating the MP3."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Tom's Diner

facts.title: Re-edition
facts.body: This is a re-edition of A Certain Ratio's 1981 album, phonetically referred to as "Tugee" or "tu H" in the transcript. The original 1981 release was considered a standout album in the Post-Punk genre, which experienced an "incredible year" in 1981. Although perhaps not as widely remembered today as Joy Division, it was a very significant contribution to the Post-Punk scene. "Y se redita a un disco de Acerter in Rathio, tu H, de 1981, 1981 fue uno de los años más increíbles del Postpank y uno de los grandes discos que tuvimos en 1988 fue este Tugee de Acerter in Rathio, que no está recordado ahora mejor como yo de division, pero fue un grandísimo al mundo del Postpank."
facts.source: Music Radar Clan

facts.body: The lead single from "Ghost in the Machine," this deeply romantic song became The Police's first "true pop smash," rising to number three on the Hot 100 by the fall of 1981, marking their highest charting hit to date. Sting wrote an early version in 1977 while secretly falling in love with his future wife, Trudy Styler, while still married to his first wife, Francis Tomlty, capturing the feeling of helpless infatuation. Four years later, in collaboration with Copeland, Summers, and producer Hugh Padgham, it gained a lush, uptempo sound, blending Caribbean and new wave elements. Its video, shot in Montserrat, received extensive MTV play and immediate radio rotation. "Every little thing she does is magic. It was a deeply romantic song, but it was not a new song. Sting wrote an early version in 1977 when he was covertly falling in love with his future wife Trudy Styler while married to his first wife, Francis Tomlty."
facts.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
facts.episode: If You Love Sting, Set Him Free Edition Part 1

facts.body: A seminal moment for hip-hop culture in the mainstream, "Rapture" began climbing the charts while "The Tide Is High" was still at number one. It featured a bizarre rap break penned by Chris Stein and Debbie Harry, shouting out Fab 5 Freddy and Grandmaster Flash, and telling a "loopy tale of a man from Mars eating cars." Keyboardist Jimmy Destry added tubular bells, and the rhythm section contributed a post-disco groove. It quickly reached number one just eight weeks after its debut, completing Blondie's "quad-fecta" of number one songs in four different styles between 1979 and 1981, and also peaked at number 33 on Billboard's Soul Singles chart. "Just eight weeks after it debuted, Rapture was number one."
facts.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
facts.episode: This Ain’t No Party! Edition Part 2

facts.title: Political Inspiration, Musical Characteristics, and Chart Performance
facts.body: The song "Whip It" was intended by a figure referred to as "Mother's Boss" to provide a critique or "kick in the butt" to President Jimmy Carter. This was motivated by Mother's Boss's concern that Ronald Reagan would win the 1980 election, which ultimately occurred. Musically, the song is described as simultaneously nonsensical, disoriented, and catchy, proving to be an annoyance to parents. It also served as a significant bridge, connecting the prevailing sounds of the 1970s with the emerging synth-driven pop music of the 1980s. Originating from the Ohio band Devo, "Whip It" achieved a peak position of number 14 on the Billboard Hot 100 chart in 1981. "The song is all at once nonsensical, disoriented, catchy, and annoyance to parents and a bridge from the sounds of the 70s to the synth driven pop of the 80s."
facts.source: For the Record - The 70s
facts.episode: Ep. 43 - Music and The Kent State Massacre of May 4, 1970
facts.name: Whip It

facts.title: Formation and Lineup Changes (1981)
facts.body: Parálisis Permanente was formed in 1981, initially including brothers Eduardo and Javier Benavente, along with Nacho and Johnny Canut. Javier Benavente later left the band, and Ana Curra joined, bringing her distinctive keyboard sound. "La banda se formó en 1981 para Lelo Apegamo y des, con los hermanos Eduardo y Javier benavente por un lado y Nacho y Johnny Canut por otro. Finalmente Javier abandonó la banda y se les unió a Nakura."
facts.source: Central Sonora
facts.episode: La España Siniestra ｜ La edad de oro del Postpunk y el Dark wave
facts.name: Parálisis Permanente

facts.title: Formation of "Onda Siniestra" Pioneer (1981)
facts.body: Décima Víctima formed in 1981, becoming another major band of the initial phase of the "onda siniestra" in Spain. Their sound was described as extremely cold and dark, drawing parallels to Joy Division. "Al igual que para el Isis permanente y Gabinete Caligari, en 1981 también se formó la otra gran banda de la primera etapa de la onda siniestra, décima víctima."
facts.source: Central Sonora
facts.episode: La España Siniestra ｜ La edad de oro del Postpunk y el Dark wave
facts.name: Décima Víctima

facts.body: The Go-Go's debut album, *Beauty and the Beat*, achieved the number 1 position on the charts. This was a historically significant accomplishment as it marked the first time that an all-female rock band had reached the number 1 spot on the album charts. "the album made it to number 1. Incredibly the first time that an all-female rock band accomplished that."
facts.source: For the Record - The 70s
facts.name: Beauty and the Beat

facts.body: Released in 1981, this album is considered the band's best-selling record. It achieved significant sales, approximately one million copies in Canada, five million in the US, and many more worldwide. The album produced several major rock radio hits, including "Tom Sawyer" and "YYZ." "I think 1981's Moving Pictures is the band's best selling record."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

facts.body: Released in September 1981, this single by Depeche Mode was highlighted as a perfect representation of the Technopop sound that was emerging and gaining popularity. It encapsulated the electronic-driven style that became a hallmark of the era. "The best mode and their third single just can't get enough. That was released in September 1981 and is perfectly representative of the sound that became known as Technopop."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
